posts.title: Wild PC
posts.description: Software Needs a Home # You may have hear the term “ Vibe Coding ”. It just means writing software with AI assistants. You can ask most assistants to write code for you presently and they’ll do a fair job of it. There’s some serious work to be done , still, in getting them to write good software, but, really it’s already good enough form many types of software.

posts.title: The Dream of Personal Computers
posts.description: The Dream # I want to talk about you and me, and our, and our society’s relationship with technology. But allow me to start with a touch of history. In 1936, mathematician Alan Turing conceived of theoretical machines that could be generally configured and reconfigured to operate in nearly infinite ways. He called these “Universal Turing Machines” because he imagined them being repurposed universally for any desired procedural calculation. Hundreds of years earlier people were programming looms and player pianos to weave fabric and play music, but Turing showed that programs of abstract, symbolic language could be used by general purpose machines to execute any procedure. Within a decade, groups in Britain and the United States cobbled together the world’s first computers. Turing expected machines to eventually learn, discover, strategize, and adapt. posts.title: Design Intelligence
posts.description: A lot of my recent thoughts about coding with agents lately (like this , and this , and this ) have been circling a specific topic… design. Coding agents are now good enough to replace all of my manual coding tasks, I haven’t written code myself for months (and it’s not because I don’t know how), but we’re still figuring out how to make them better at the more “senior” software development tasks.
